items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And then I would do some gigs with Lee and Archie every now and then.

ctx.x: So, when you brought up Lee Morgan, Bobby Timmons, what I’m thinking is, that’s a lot of blues . . . a lot of gospel. And when I look at your biography on your website, the first thing it says is, “Shaping modern jazz, Tyner’s blues-based piano style.” So were you listening to the blues early on, was that part of that foundation?

Yeah, you had to because blues singers had a lot of the gigs. If you wanted to get the jobs . . . If people wanted to throw a party, they may use a local club to do that because there were drinks there and they may even get a caterer to cater to it. So all of that was a part of it and I enjoyed participating in that. People would come and have a good time, you know? And then I would do some gigs with Lee and Archie every now and then.
Jimmy Vass was also another one. Him and Archie were close.
